extracted.intended_audience: authors, researchers, journal editors and reviewers preparing or evaluating reports of randomized controlled trials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing complete, transparent reports of randomized (parallel-group) clinical trials, including checklists and diagrams to document design, conduct, analysis, and participant flow. Includes extensions and complementary guidance for specific trial designs, data types, and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An evidence-based, minimum set of recommendations for reporting randomized trials; offers a standard way for authors to prepare reports of trial findings, facilitating complete and transparent reporting, reducing bias, and aiding critical appraisal and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement is intended as the principal guideline for reporting randomized trials and should be used to prepare trial reports. It is part of the EQUATOR Network initiative. Consider the Statement the core standard to follow when writing trial reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT 2010 checklist (25-item)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most recent version (2010) consists of a 25-item checklist and a participant flow diagram. The checklist items focus on reporting how the trial was designed, analyzed, and interpreted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should address each of the 25 checklist items in their report. The checklist provides the minimum information to include; journals endorsing CONSORT expect these items to be reported. The flow diagram should display the progress of all participants through the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT Explanation and Elaboration document
rubrics_metrics.description: A companion document that explains and illustrates the principles underlying the CONSORT Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended that authors use the Explanation and Elaboration document in conjunction with the CONSORT Statement for guidance, examples, and clarifications about how to report each checklist item.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT 2025 updates (open-science additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An updated 'CONSORT 2025' checklist (superseding 2010) that adds seven items, revises three, removes one, and introduces a new open-science section covering trial registration, protocol/SAP access, data sharing, and disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should refer to the updated 2025 checklist where applicable; new items emphasize registration, access to protocols/statistical analysis plans (SAPs), data sharing, and disclosure practices to enhance transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the most up-to-date CONSORT version
rubrics_metrics.description: The CONSORT Statement is considered an evolving document and is subject to periodic changes as new evidence emerges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users of the guideline are strongly recommended to refer to and apply the most up-to-date version of CONSORT when writing or interpreting trial reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagram that displays the progress of all participants through the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a flow diagram in trial reports to show enrollment, allocation, follow-up, and analysis numbers for transparency about participant flow and attrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT extensions for specific trial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions developed to give additional guidance for randomized trials with specific designs (e.g., cluster randomized trials, factorial trials, noninferiority and equivalence trials, pragmatic trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a trial uses a specific design, authors should use the corresponding CONSORT extension (rather than or in addition to the core checklist) to ensure design-specific reporting requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT extensions for specific data types and reporting elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions that address particular reporting elements or data types, for example reporting of harms and reporting in abstracts; also CONSORT-Surrogate for surrogate endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the applicable extension (e.g., CONSORT for harms, CONSORT for abstracts, CONSORT-Surrogate) to ensure complete reporting of these specific elements. Extensions provide tailored checklist items and elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT extensions for types of interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions and elaborations that offer guidance for reporting trials of specific intervention types (e.g., herbal interventions, non-pharmacologic treatments, acupuncture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For trials of special intervention types, use the relevant CONSORT extension (e.g., STRICTA for acupuncture) or elaborated CONSORT guidance to provide adequate intervention description and other intervention-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary guidance: TIDieR and TIDieR-Placebo
rubrics_metrics.description: TIDieR encourages adequate descriptions of interventions; TIDieR-Placebo encourages adequate descriptions of placebo or sham controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use TIDieR (and TIDieR-Placebo when relevant) alongside CONSORT to ensure interventions (and controls) are described in sufficient detail to allow replication and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt evidence-based reporting practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT is evidence-based and its use has been associated with improved reporting of randomized trials; it is widely endorsed by journals and editorial groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and journals should adopt CONSORT items because they are empirically informed practices intended to reduce bias and improve transparency; endorsement by journals signals expected reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select complementary reporting standards when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Other reporting guidelines (e.g., STROBE, STARD, STREGA, PRISMA, TRIPOD+AI, SQUIRE) exist for study types other than randomized trials and for complementary reporting needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a study includes elements or methods covered by other reporting guidelines, authors should consult and apply those complementary standards in addition to CONSORT to cover all relevant reporting domains.
